newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen weak ahead of central bank data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen weak ahead of central bank data.

text.p: Thai stocks are seen weak ahead of a release of central bank data due later on Thursday and the resumption of trading in the stock of currently suspended Finance One Plc on Friday, analysts said.
The SET Index closed 7.01 points lower at 562.83 on Wednesday. The SET 50 shed 0.59 points to 40.69.

"I still believe it is on a downward trend ... At the moment there is very little long-term investment because of the economy is yet to show signs of turning around at the moment we can only advise people to invest for short term speculation," said a senior researcher at IFCT Finance and Securities Plc.
Early trade is expected to be sluggish ahead of an economic data release from the central bank later today, analysts said.
"I think the figures may show some signs of improvement at the macro-level, but on the micro-level I think things are getting worse," the analyst said.
The resumption of trade in troubled Finance One on Friday is also likely to weigh on sentiment as the event is widely tipped to pull the market down, analysts said.
Thailand's sluggish economic outlook underpins market sentiment with concerns growing that some manufacturers and industrial firms are face growing difficulties, they added.
